notes_for_editor: Only the tnlandforms entry (WET001) and statewide Division of Forestry context were found. Two web searches and the NRHP and FFLA documents named no Gleason tower in Weakley County. The code GD1498 is not explained on the page; the record lists it as an NGS register number, and the story does not interpret it. The Gleason Mountain lookout in Pend Oreille County, Washington, is a different tower and was not used. Unread lead: a Gleason town history, Gleason: A Look Back (1986), named on a Weakley County genealogy page. The MPS says TDF 'constructed' 208 towers ca. 1930 to ca. 1970 in one place and 'oversaw' 208 at its peak in another; the story uses the peak wording. The FFLA total of 275 built differs from the MPS peak of 208; the story says so and does not reconcile them. No NHLR or FFLOS register page for this tower was found in the local cache.
